examples.ko: 정말 고마워요. 다음에 제가 밥 살게요.
examples.en: Thank you so much. I'll buy you a meal next time.
Thanks for helping. The work finished early.

examples.ko: 어제 선물 고마워요. 아주 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: Thanks for the gift yesterday. I really like it.
Thank you for always being by my side.
Thanks for letting me know. I understand now.

examples.ko: 와 주셔서 고마워요. 오늘 정말 즐거웠어요.
examples.en: Thank you for coming. I had a great time today.

explain: '고맙다'의 해요체예요. 친구나 동료, 아랫사람에게 편하고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요. 어른께는 '감사합니다'나 '고맙습니다'가 더 공손해요. 친한 친구끼리는 '고마워'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Thank you for helping me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이나 처음 보는 사람에게 쓰는 공손한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to thank elders or people you have just met.

phrases.en: Thanks for the gift. It's really pretty.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for close friends or younger people.

phrases.en: Thank you so much. It really helped.
phrases.nuance_ko: '너무'를 붙여서 고마운 마음을 더 크게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding an intensifier makes the gratitude sound bigger.

explain_en: It is the 해요-style form of '고맙다'. Use it with friends, coworkers and younger people in a soft, friendly way. To elders, '감사합니다' or '고맙습니다' is more polite. Close friends say '고마워'.

examples.en: I got a present, said 'Thank you,' and smiled.
As I left the shop, I said 'Thank you' to the clerk.
I teach my child how to say 'Thank you.'

examples.ko: 버스에서 내릴 때 기사님께 고맙습니다 하고 말해요.
examples.en: When I get off the bus, I say thank you to the driver.

examples.ko: 친구에게 보낸 편지 끝에 고맙습니다라고 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote 'Thank you' at the end of the letter to my friend.
To an elder, you should say 'Gomapseumnida' instead of 'Gomawo.'

explain: '고맙다'는 순우리말이고 '감사하다'는 한자어예요. '고맙습니다'는 일상에서 편하게, '감사합니다'는 조금 더 격식 있는 자리에서 많이 써요. 친구에게는 '고마워', 부드럽게는 '고마워요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Thank you for helping me.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more relaxed tone than the main phrase.

phrases.en: To a friend, you say 'Thanks.'
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for friends and close people.

phrases.en: Thank you for the gift. I'll use it well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고맙습니다'보다 조금 더 격식 있는 자리에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in slightly more formal situations.

explain_en: '고맙다' is a native Korean word, while '감사하다' is Sino-Korean. '고맙습니다' is common in everyday life, and '감사합니다' is often used in more formal settings. With friends say '고마워', and for a softer polite tone '고마워요'.

examples.en: Thanks for the gift! It's really pretty.
Thanks for giving me water. I was thirsty.

examples.ko: 오늘 정말 고마워. 내일 또 만나자.
examples.en: Thanks so much for today. Let's meet again tomorrow.
Thanks for coming. I'm really happy.
Thanks, my friend, for always being there.
Thanks for lending me this book. It's fun.

explain: 친구나 동생에게 쓰는 반말이에요. 뒤에 '요'를 붙인 '고마워요'는 부드러운 존댓말이지만, 어른께는 '고맙습니다'나 '감사합니다'가 더 안전해요. '고맙다'는 ㅂ 불규칙이라 ㅂ이 '우'로 바뀌어 '고마워'가 돼요.

phrases.en: Thank you for helping me.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer polite form of the casual headword.

phrases.en: Teacher, thank you for helping me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이나 처음 보는 사람에게 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal form for elders or people you've just met.

phrases.en: Thank you for being with me yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 일에 고마움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to thank someone for something that already happened.

explain_en: '고마워' is casual speech for friends or younger people. Adding '요' ('고마워요') makes it soft and polite, but to elders '고맙습니다' or '감사합니다' is safer. '고맙다' is a ㅂ-irregular verb: the ㅂ turns into '우', giving '고마워'.

examples.ko: 면접이 끝나고 '시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다'라고 인사했어요.
examples.en: After the interview ended, I said, 'Thank you for making time.'

examples.ko: 메일 마지막에 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다라고 썼어요.
examples.en: At the end of the email I wrote, 'Thank you for making time.'

examples.ko: 회의에 온 분들께 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다 하고 말했어요.
examples.en: I told the people who came to the meeting, 'Thank you for making time.'

examples.ko: 바쁜 손님께는 헤어질 때 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다라고 해요.
examples.en: To a busy guest, I say 'Thank you for making time' when we part.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 사회자가 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다라고 말했어요.
examples.en: Before the presentation, the host said, 'Thank you for making time.'

examples.ko: 선생님께 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다라는 카드를 드렸어요.
examples.en: I gave the teacher a card saying 'Thank you for making time.'

explain: 바쁜 사람이 나를 위해 시간을 써 준 것에 고마워할 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '시간을 내다'는 일부러 시간을 만든다는 말이고, '시간이 나다'는 저절로 여유가 생긴다는 말이라서 서로 달라요. 동료에게는 '시간 내 줘서 고마워요'처럼 편하게 말해요.

phrases.en: Thank you for making time even though you're busy.
phrases.nuance_en: A relaxed version for colleagues or friends.

phrases.en: Thank you for coming today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 모임에 온 사람에게 하는 격식 있는 인사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal thank-you to people who came to an event or meeting.

phrases.en: Thank you for helping me even though you're busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 바쁜 것을 알고 있다는 마음을 담아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that you know the other person is busy.
phrases.en_equiv: thank you despite your busy schedule

explain_en: It is a formal way to thank a busy person for spending time on you. '시간을 내다' means to deliberately make time, while '시간이 나다' means free time happens to open up, so they differ. With a colleague you can say it more casually, like '시간 내 줘서 고마워요'.

en: Thank you for the meal (said before eating)

examples.ko: 밥을 먹기 전에 “잘 먹겠습니다” 하고 말해요.
examples.en: Before eating, I say “thank you for the meal”.

examples.ko: 어머니가 차려 주신 밥에 “잘 먹겠습니다”라고 인사했어요.
examples.en: I said “thank you for the meal” for the food my mother prepared.
I answered “thank you for the meal” and picked up my spoon.

examples.ko: 선배가 밥을 사 주면 “잘 먹겠습니다”라고 말해요.
examples.en: When a senior buys me a meal, I say “thank you for the meal”.

examples.ko: 식당에서 음식이 나오면 “잘 먹겠습니다” 하고 먹기 시작해요.
examples.en: When the food arrives at a restaurant, I say “thank you” and start eating.

examples.ko: 회식 자리에서 사장님께 잘 먹겠습니다 하고 인사했어요.
examples.en: At the company dinner, I thanked the boss before eating.

explain: 밥을 먹기 전에, 특히 밥을 차려 주거나 사 준 사람에게 하는 인사예요. 식사 후에는 '잘 먹었습니다'로 이어서 말해요. 친한 사이에서는 '잘 먹을게요'나 '잘 먹을게'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Thank you. I'll enjoy this.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than '잘 먹겠습니다', for people you're close to.

phrases.en: Mom, thanks for the food!
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for family and friends.

phrases.en: I will enjoy this meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘 먹겠습니다'처럼 공손하지만 맛있게 먹겠다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As polite as '잘 먹겠습니다', adding that you'll enjoy the food.

explain_en: This is said before eating, especially to the person who cooked or paid for the meal. After the meal you follow it with '잘 먹었습니다'. Among close friends, people say '잘 먹을게요' or '잘 먹을게'.

examples.en: After finishing the meal, I said “thank you for the meal”.

examples.ko: 맛있게 먹은 후 사장님께 “잘 먹었습니다” 하고 말했어요.
examples.en: After enjoying the food, I said “thank you for the meal” to the owner.
If you say “thank you for the meal”, the cook is happy.

examples.ko: 선배가 계산해 주셔서 “잘 먹었습니다” 하고 감사 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: My senior paid, so I thanked him with “thank you for the meal”.

examples.ko: 식당을 나서며 직원에게 잘 먹었습니다 하고 웃었어요.
examples.en: As I left the restaurant, I smiled and said thanks to the staff.

examples.ko: 어머니께 잘 먹었습니다 하고 말한 뒤 설거지를 했어요.
examples.en: I said thanks to my mother for the meal and then did the dishes.

explain: 식사를 마친 뒤 대접해 준 사람이나 식당 사람에게 하는 인사예요. 식사 전에는 '잘 먹겠습니다'를 써서 앞뒤 쌍으로 기억하면 쉬워요. 친한 사이에서는 '잘 먹었어요'나 '잘 먹었어'라고 해요.

phrases.en: It was delicious. Thank you for the meal.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, everyday polite form of '잘 먹었습니다'.

phrases.en: Mom, thanks for the meal!
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for friends and family.

phrases.en: I enjoyed the meal. Thank you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 맛있었다는 마음을 더 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: It shows more clearly that you enjoyed the food.

explain_en: You say this after a meal to the host or restaurant staff. It pairs with '잘 먹겠습니다' before eating, so remember them as a set. Among close friends, people say '잘 먹었어요' or '잘 먹었어'.

examples.ko: 민수 씨, 생일 축하해요. 오늘 케이크 먹어요.
examples.en: Minsu, happy birthday. Let's eat cake today.

examples.ko: 회사 동료에게 웃으며 생일 축하해요 하고 말했어요.
examples.en: I smiled and said happy birthday to my coworker.
I sent my friend a text saying “happy birthday”.
Happy belated birthday. I also prepared a present.

examples.ko: 다 같이 촛불을 끄며 생일 축하해요!
examples.en: Let's blow out the candles together and say happy birthday!

examples.ko: 수지 씨 생일이 오늘이죠? 생일 축하해요!
examples.en: Today is your birthday, Suji, right? Happy birthday!

explain: 동료나 아는 사이에게 쓰는 부드러운 축하 인사예요. 어른께는 '생신 축하드립니다'나 '생일 축하드려요'라고 해요. 친한 친구에게는 '생일 축하해'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Happy birthday! Here's a gift for you.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for close friends or younger people.

phrases.en: Happy birthday, teacher.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite form for people older or higher than you.

phrases.example: 생일 축하해요! 오늘 행복한 하루 보내요.
phrases.en: Happy birthday! Have a happy day today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생일 인사 뒤에 덧붙이면 더 따뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding this after the birthday greeting makes it warmer.

explain_en: This is a gentle birthday greeting for coworkers or acquaintances. To elders you say '생신 축하드립니다' or '생일 축하드려요'. To close friends you say '생일 축하해'.

examples.en: Thank you, teacher.
A present? Thank you so much.
Here's your coffee. — Thank you.
Are you all right? — Yes, thank you.
Thank you, driver.

explain: 감사합니다는 가게, 회사, 모르는 사람에게 모두 쓸 수 있어요. 친구에게는 “고마워”라고 해요. “고맙습니다”도 같은 뜻이에요.
explain_en: 감사합니다 is safe in shops, at work and with strangers. With friends say 고마워. 고맙습니다 means the same thing.

examples.en: Happy birthday!
I sent my sister a birthday message.
My friend got a job, so we all celebrated.

examples.ko: 결혼을 축하해 주러 많은 사람이 왔어요.
examples.en: Many people came to congratulate them on their wedding.
I bought a bouquet to congratulate them on graduating.
Teacher, congratulations on your promotion!

explain: '생일 축하해요', '합격 축하해요'처럼 축하할 일 뒤에 바로 써요. 웃어른께는 '축하드려요'라고 말해요. '축하해 주다'는 상대를 위해 해 주는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It follows the occasion directly, as in '생일 축하해요' and '합격 축하해요'. To someone senior, say '축하드려요'. '축하해 주다' adds a feeling of doing it for the other person.

examples.en: Two tickets, please.
Three T-shirts for 10,000 won.
I take four photos.
One receipt, please.
Two postcards are 1,000 won.

explain: 종이처럼 얇고 평평한 것은 ‘장’으로 세어요. 종이, 표, 사진, 엽서가 그래요.

explain_en: Thin, flat things like paper are counted with 장: paper, tickets, photos, postcards.

examples.en: I bought flowers as a birthday present for my friend.
What would be a good birthday present for my mother?
Please gift-wrap it.
I got a birthday present and felt happy.
Who are you going to give this present to?

explain_en: To an elder you say 선물을 드려요; to a friend, 선물을 줘요.

usage: 그거 = spoken short form of 그것.

examples.en: What's that?
That one by you is my bag.
Is that a Korean book?
Is that coffee? — Yes, it's coffee.
That is my friend's umbrella.

explain: 그거는 듣는 사람 가까이에 있는 물건뿐 아니라, 방금 들은 이야기도 가리켜요. 그래서 대화에서 아주 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 식당 좀 비싸죠? — 그건 그래요.
phrases.en: That's true; I'll give you that.
phrases.nuance_en: said when you partly agree with what the other person said
phrases.en_equiv: That's true; I'll give you that.

explain_en: 그거 points to something near the listener, but also to something that was just mentioned in the conversation. That is why it shows up so often in speech.
